problema.title: Choosing software shouldn't turn into a gamble
problema.intro: A company may know it needs to modernize, but questions pile up: Do we need a new ERP or should we optimize the current one? Which CRM actually fits our sales process? Will our HR system support our growth? Which asset management solution can integrate with our architecture?
problema.punch: Every vendor presents their solution as the answer. The organization ends up with a lot of information, but not necessarily an objective decision.

bullets: Processes that have to bend to the software
costo.punch: The cost of choosing wrong isn't just buying the wrong software. It's everything that happens after.

closingQuote: We don't recommend technology off a catalog. Our job isn't to sell a particular platform. We evaluate the available alternatives and build a recommendation based on each organization's needs, priorities, and context. 100% technology-agnostic.

items.question: What is enterprise software selection and how does it work?
items.answer: It is the process of deciding which platform fits the company by comparing several alternatives against criteria defined before any demo. At Cyrrus it follows five steps: understand the business, map the processes, turn them into requirements, evaluate the technology and, last, choose the vendor. We start from the business, not the vendor's catalog.

items.question: When should a company hire a software selection consultant?
items.answer: When it has to decide whether to replace or modernize an ERP, CRM, HCM, or EAM and has demos, proposals, and internal opinions, but no criteria to compare them. Also when there is already a preferred vendor and the decision should be validated against objective criteria before signing.

items.question: Is the evaluation really vendor-agnostic?
items.answer: Yes. We have no commercial partnerships or commissions with ERP, CRM, HCM, EAM, or other enterprise software vendors — we evaluate against the same objective criteria regardless of brand.

items.question: How long does an enterprise software selection process take?
items.answer: As a reference, the Identify phase of the CIRA method takes 6 to 12 weeks, from strategic kickoff to contracting support, and includes criteria definition, the RFP, proposal evaluation, and vendor reference checks.

items.question: What if the right software is the one we already have?
items.answer: That is a valid outcome and it does happen. If the evaluation concludes your current platform meets the defined criteria, the recommendation is to optimize it rather than replace it: we have no commercial incentive for you to buy anything new.

items.question: Who from our team should take part in the selection?
items.answer: The owners of the processes the tool will support, an IT counterpart, and a sponsor with budget authority. In our view, end users should take part from the criteria-definition stage: that way the evaluation covers usability and adoption starts early.

respuesta.title: What is enterprise software selection?
respuesta.body: It is the process of defining what the company needs to solve, turning it into criteria and requirements, and comparing several platforms against them before signing with a vendor.
